subject: Post-call: Cloudbridge competitive parity plan & next tests
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Cloudbridge competitive parity plan & next tests

Hi Karen —

Thanks again for the 45-minute demo call this morning. Quick recap from my side and the concrete next steps we discussed so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements you emphasized:
- Reliable streaming of assistant responses into your UI with consumer-grade reconnect behavior
- Deterministic structured outputs for order/fulfillment events (JSON Schema validation)
- Robust function/tool-calling semantics for third-party backend orchestrations
- Predictable latency and cost compared to what you’re seeing from the hyperscalers (especially for 256–1024 token responses)

How Redwood differentiates (high level):
- Streaming: protocol supports chunked streaming with reconnect + resume semantics and configurable prefix caching to reduce cold-start latency
- Structured output: first-class schema enforcement and a strict-mode option that returns validation errors as metadata so you can auto-retry instead of parsing failures
- Function/tool calling: durable invocation model with at-least-once delivery and idempotency hints; SDK has helpers to materialize tool responses into events
- Cost controls: batching + KV cache recommendations we can tune per-workload to reduce token costs while preserving latency SLOs

Proposed PoC tests (we agreed on 2–3 quick, measurable checks):
1) Streaming behavior: 500 sessions, intermittent network drops (5% churn) — measure reconnection/resume success and mean time-to-first-chunk
2) Function calling reliability: 1k invocations wired to a stubbed backend (idempotency keys) — measure duplicate deliveries and end-to-end latency
3) Structured-output strictness: 200 prompts with edge-case inputs; validate strict-mode vs permissive-mode outputs against your schema
4) Baseline throughput/latency run: 512 tokens, cold vs warm cache, compute cost per 1k tokens (Redwood vs hyperscaler A sample numbers)

Attachments: I’m including the PoC scope doc and a short performance snapshot from our internal runs for reference. Also attaching a sample prompt set (JSONL) for the structured-output tests.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm a technical contact for your SRE / platform team (we can add them to the test harness access)
- Confirm whether you want Redwood-hosted models or a Private deployment for the PoC (hosted is fastest)
- Any compliance constraints (data residency / audit logs) we should bake into the setup

If that looks right I’ll loop Dylan to scope the exact test harness and schedule a 30–45 minute kickoff next week. We can run the first streaming test within 72 hours after we have credentials.

Thanks —
Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0123

Thanks for the recap and the clear test plan. Looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 
- SRE contact: please loop in Antonio Mendez (antonio.m@cloudbridge.com) for network/egress policy and credentials (I copied him on a separate invite).
- For PoC hosting: we’d prefer Redwood-hosted to move faster, but we need to validate data residency (must stay in us-west region) — let us know if that’s possible.

One question: on structured outputs — can you confirm whether your strict-mode returns non-200s for schema-mismatches or returns 200 with validation metadata? We need deterministic behavior to drive an automated retry flow.

Happy to proceed. Antonio will be the SRE contact — I’ll put him in the kickoff.

Dylan —

Forwarding the note from Cloudbridge (Karen). They accepted the plan and want Redwood-hosted PoC in us-west if possible. Budget note: ~$25k two-week PoC. Please scope a minimal harness that covers the four tests in the original email.

Key asks to cover in the scope: 
- Streaming: reiterate session count (500), network churn simulation (5%), metrics to capture (time-to-first-chunk, chunk-rate, resume-success-rate)
- Function calling: at-least-once detection and de-dup metrics; include idempotency-key header behavior and sample back-end stubbing we can provide
- Structured outputs: we need strict-mode behavior that returns validation metadata (not just a 200 with freeform string). Karen specifically asked whether strict-mode uses 200+metadata or 4xx. Please specify what Redwood returns and include an option in the harness to flip modes.
- Baseline latency/cost: 512 token response, cold vs warm cache, and a simple cost-per-1k-tokens calc. We should include a comparable hyperscaler run (Bedrock-equivalent / Hyperscale-A) as a side-by-side.

Attachments: sample-prompt-set.jsonl (edge-case prompts for schema validation). Can you also prepare an initial runbook and list of credentials we’ll need from Cloudbridge (API key, region, optional VPC peering info) so we can send a short checklist to Karen and Antonio?

If you can drop a proposed test schedule and resource estimate today, I’ll send it to Karen and lock the kickoff.

Thanks —
Camila

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 12:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Cloudbridge competitive parity plan & next tests

Camila / Marissa —

Thanks — I sketched a minimal test harness and schedule below. I’ll stand up the initial jobs if you approve.

Planned test harness (high level):
A) Streaming experiment
- Workload: 500 simultaneous sessions, typical prompt -> 512 token response distribution.
- Failure injection: random TCP drops on 5% of sessions at t=5–15s.
- Metrics: time-to-first-chunk, resume-success-rate, median chunk inter-arrival, end-to-end completion rate.
- Redwood config: streaming=true, prefix-cache=on, resume-window=30s.
- Duration: 3 hours (warm-up + 2 sustained runs)

B) Function calling reliability
- Workload: 1,000 invocations with idempotency keys; backend stub replies with 200 after 150–600ms.
- Metrics: duplicate deliveries, median end-to-end latency, success-rate.
- Redwood config: at_least_once_guard=true, ack-window=auto.
- Duration: 1 hour (burst + steady)

C) Structured-output strictness
- Workload: 200 edge-case prompts from sample-prompt-set.jsonl.
- Modes: strict-mode (returns 200 + validation metadata) and permissive-mode (200 with freeform). We will validate schema failures client-side using our validator and record whether Redwood returned a validation hint.
- Deliverable: histogram of validation errors per mode + example payloads for automated-retry logic.

D) Baseline latency/cost comparison
- Baseline prompt set: 1000 requests @ 512 tokens. Compare: Redwood-hosted model (rdl-v1), Hyperscaler-A equivalent (Hyperscaler-bedrock-sim) — same concurrency and instance class where possible.
- Metrics: median latency (p50/p95), cost-per-1k-tokens (estimated), throughput (req/s).
- Deliverable: CSV with raw metrics + a short recommendation on quantization/batching settings to hit Cloudbridge latency targets.

Estimated effort / timeline / resources:
- Setup & validation: 1 engineer (me) — 1 day to stand up harness + sample scripts
- Runs & collection: 2 days (including retries and sanity checks)
- Analysis & report: 1 day to produce a short results brief and recommendations
- Total calendar: ~4 business days from credentials ready.

Credentials + checklist we’ll need to send Cloudbridge:
- API key for Redwood-hosted test account (we’ll provide temporary creds)
- Preferred region (must be us-west)
- Optional: VPC peering details (if they want private connectivity)
- Contact: Antonio Mendez (SRE) for network verification

Next actions I’ll take today if you greenlight:
- Prepare harness repo and the initial run scripts and share a short doc link
- Share a one-page runbook + credential checklist with Karen and Antonio
- Schedule the kickoff (30–45min) with Cloudbridge for Monday morning PST

Happy to refine. Once we get the explicit go from Karen/Antonio I’ll spin up the first streaming run.

—Dylan Brooks
